en.body:
The allure of **Outer Banks** has always been tied to its sun-drenched, windswept coastal aesthetic, promising adventure on the fictional Kildare Island. However, the journey to bring this Pogue paradise to life involved a surprising amount of travel and clever location scouting, often far from the North Carolina coast the show purports to represent. For the first three seasons, the lush, marshy lowcountry of South Carolina, particularly around **Charleston**, served as the primary stand-in for the OBX. Spots like **Shem Creek** and the historic **Secessionville Historic District** masterfully mimicked the North Carolina barrier islands, immersing viewers in the world of treasure hunts and family feuds.

As the Pogues' quest for gold escalated from local shipwrecks to legendary lost cities, so did the production's ambition. Season 2 saw the crew jetting off to **Barbados**, where the vibrant streets of Bridgetown, including the iconic **Careenage** area and the luxurious **Fairmont Hotel**, doubled for the sun-drenched locales of the Bahamas. This international flair continued into Season 3, with locations hinting at the mythical jungles of South America, further expanding the show's visual scope and the stakes of their global pursuit.

## A Global Treasure Hunt

By Season 4, **Outer Banks** finally touched down in the real North Carolina for specific sequences, notably the high-octane Enduro dirt bike race. Simultaneously, the production pushed the boundaries of "Pogue hell" with a grueling, cinematic shoot that ventured into the desert dunes and historic medinas of **Morocco**. This starkly contrasted the familiar coastal settings, showcasing the crew's willingness to explore diverse and challenging environments to serve the narrative's escalating drama and adventure.

## The Adriatic Finale

The fifth and final season concluded the Pogues' ultimate globe-trotting adventure in the Mediterranean. Swapping the Atlantic shoals for the Adriatic coast, production set up shop in **Croatia**. The UNESCO-protected medieval streets of **Dubrovnik**, the rugged cliffs of **Danče Beach**, and the lush nature reserve of **Lokrum Island** provided an epic, jaw-dropping backdrop for the series' climactic moments, offering a visually stunning and historically rich setting for the Pogues' final quest.

## What's Next

While the on-screen adventures of the Pogues have concluded, the legacy of **Outer Banks** as a global phenomenon continues. Fans eager to revisit these stunning filming locations can now trace the steps of John B and his crew across South Carolina, Barbados, Morocco, and Croatia, experiencing the real-world magic behind the show's fictional treasure map.

Courtesy of Netflix © 2026 Netflix’s hit treasure-hunting series Outer Banks has finally come to a close after five huge seasons, taking us on a wild ride from the marshy coastlines of Kildare Island to the far reaches of the globe. As die-hard fans know, the biggest behind-the-scenes secret of the show’s early days is that the “OBX” wasn’t actually filmed in North Carolina. Due to inclusivity concerns over a controversial bathroom bill during the show’s early development, production instead set up shop in Charleston, South Carolina. For the first three seasons, the stunning Lowcountry—including spots like Mount Pleasant’s Shem Creek, Kiawah Island, and the historic Secessionville Historic District—perfectly doubled for the North Carolina barrier islands. As John B and the Pogues’ hunt for gold escalated from local shipwrecks to legendary lost cities, the production’s footprint had to evolve, too. The series quickly went international, with the gorgeous island of Barbados stepping in to double for the sun-drenched streets of the Bahamas in Season 2, as well as the mythical jungles of South America in Season 3. By Season 4, the crew finally made their way to the real North Carolina to film the high-stakes Enduro dirt bike race, while simultaneously pushing the boundaries of “Pogue hell” with a grueling, cinematic shoot in the desert dunes and historic medinas of Morocco. For the fifth and final season, the Pogues took their ultimate globe-trotting adventure to the Mediterranean . Swapping the Atlantic shoals for the Adriatic coast, production touched down in Croatia. The UNESCO-protected medieval streets of Dubrovnik, the rugged cliffs of Danče Beach, and the lush nature reserve of Lokrum Island provided an epic, jaw-dropping backdrop for the show’s final chapter.
